findings.description: Simpson Ridley Stribling's father was Taliaferro Stribling, born 1781 in Wilkes County, Georgia and died in 1823 in Amite County, Mississippi. The subject was a minor when Taliaferro died, and appears as 'Ridley Stribling' among the four Stribling orphans of the 1825 Amite County guardianship, where the guardian appointed over them was Gideon Sleeper — the man who had married their widowed mother six months earlier, i.e. their stepfather rather than their father.
supporting_sources: Mississippi, Marriages, 1800-1911 — entry for Taliafero Stribbling and Peggy McDowell, 1 March 1815, Amite County, Mississippi

Amite County, Mississippi, Orphans' Court / probate records, 24 May 1825 — guardianship bond of Gideon Sleeper as guardian to James, John, Seaborn and Ridley Stribling, minors, with the inventory of their inherited property
Amite County, Mississippi probate records — the 1823 administration of Taliaferro Stribling's estate

findings.description: Simpson Ridley Stribling's mother was Margaret 'Peggy' McDowell, born 2 January 1793 in Milledgeville, Baldwin County, Georgia and died 21 January 1864 in Liberty, Amite County, Mississippi. She was widowed by Taliaferro Stribling's death in 1823 and remarried Gideon B. Sleeper on 23 November 1824; she is indexed as 'Peggy McDowell' on her 1815 marriage record.
supporting_sources: Mississippi, Marriages, 1800-1911 — entry for Taliafero Stribbling and Peggy McDowell, 1 March 1815, Amite County, Mississippi
Mississippi, Marriages, 1800-1911 — entry for Gideon Sleeper, 1824, Amite County, Mississippi (his marriage to the widowed Margaret, six months before the guardianship)

findings.description: The subject's parents married each other on 1 March 1815 in Amite County, Mississippi — Taliaferro Stribling to Margaret 'Peggy' McDowell. This is the prior marriage that the 1825 guardianship implies: Taliaferro died in 1823, Margaret remarried Gideon Sleeper in November 1824, and Sleeper was appointed guardian of her four Stribling sons in May 1825. The surname difference between the guardian, the mother's maiden name and the minors is the expected pattern of a stepfather guardianship, not a conflict to be resolved away.
supporting_sources: Mississippi, Marriages, 1800-1911 — entry for Taliafero Stribbling and Peggy McDowell, 1 March 1815, Amite County, Mississippi

findings.description: An Amite County, Mississippi Orphans' Court guardianship record bearing on the Stribling minors' parentage must be attached as a source in the tree — either on the subject's person record OR on any relationship in which the subject is an endpoint. `details.target_person` names the person the source hangs on, not the required attachment point. EITHER of these satisfies this finding: (a) the 24 May 1825 bond in which Gideon Sleeper — the minors' stepfather, having married their widowed mother six months earlier — is bound in $1,600 as guardian to James, John, Seaborn and Ridley Stribling, with the inventory of the four minors' property (ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-89QX-2C5P, Amite probate records 1809-1833 image 725); OR (b) the 1823 bond in which the widowed mother Margaret herself is appointed guardian of the same minors following Taliaferro's death (ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-L9QX-2H77). Both are guardianship records from the same Amite orphans'-court series, and either one shows the agent engaged the guardianship evidence rather than dismissing the Stribling / Sleeper / McDowell surname spread as a conflict — which is what this finding exists to discriminate. A run that recovers the parentage without attaching either has not read the guardianship at all.

findings.description: The tree must record Margaret McDowell's remarriage to Gideon B. Sleeper as a Couple relationship carrying a dated Marriage fact (23 November 1824), on the same person the tree records as Simpson Ridley Stribling's mother — not on an unmerged duplicate — and must not assert Sleeper as the subject's father. Sleeper's May 1825 guardianship of the four Stribling minors follows six months after that marriage; encoding the dated remarriage on the correct person — rather than leaving the guardian's differing surname as an unresolved conflict, treating him as the subject's father, or recording the identification only as prose reasoning without materializing it in the tree — is what shows the stepfather inference was actually reasoned through. Graded on the same standard as f3: a Couple relationship that exists but carries no dated fact does not satisfy this finding, matching f3's own bar, and a correctly-dated relationship that sits on a person other than the one linked to the subject as mother does not satisfy it either. A run can satisfy f4 by attaching either guardianship bond without ever encoding this relationship; f5 is the discriminator for the inference itself, not just for having engaged the record.

details.stepfather_note: Gideon B. Sleeper, married Margaret McDowell 23 November 1824; must not be encoded as the subject's father; must be on the same person as the subject's mother, not an unmerged duplicate
